Since \(n=\prod p_i^{e_i}\), we have
\[
n^n=\prod p_i^{n e_i},
\]
so
\[
\prod (n e_i+1)=861=3\cdot 7\cdot 41.
\]
Thus the factors \(n e_i+1\) must partition \(\{3,7,41\}\) into products.

Testing the possible partitions:
- \(\{21,41\}\): \(n\mid \gcd(20,40)=20\), so \(n\mid 20\). For \(n=20\), the exponents are \(1,2\), and \(20=5^1\cdot 2^2\), so this works.
- The other partitions force \(n=2\) or fail.

Check:
\[
20^{20}=(2^2\cdot 5)^{20}=2^{40}5^{20}
\]
has
\[
(40+1)(20+1)=41\cdot 21=861
\]
divisors.

\[
\boxed{20}
\]
